obligations.text: A multiply linked file under an inaccessible root refuses the launch at the hardlink step, as before.

A multiply linked file under a read-only root refuses the launch at the hardlink step when it shares its device and inode with a file under a writable directory, a writable file, or (macOS) an existing file an adjacent configuration prefix grants; otherwise it does not refuse.
When no file the child may write has more than one link, the read-only roots are not walked.

sectionHeadings: 070: A read-only root refuses only a link the child could write
record.summary: Amends spec 004 section 3.18 rule 2's alias scan. An inaccessible root still refuses any multiply linked file. A read-only root (the target's working tree, its Git directory, another attempt's workspace) refuses a multiply linked file only when another of its names lies where the child may write. Cargo's build output in a checkout and Git objects shared with a local clone no longer refuse every launch.
record.title: A read-only root refuses only a link the child could write
